scenes.title: Clive Wearing at the Upright Piano: Sight-Reading Renaissance Music Masterfully Beside His Crossed-Out '8:31 AM — NOW Awake!' Diary
scenes.era: 1995, English care suite & music room (Wilson & Wearing longitudinal study)

layout.description: Warm, sunlit British music and sitting room featuring a polished walnut upright piano holding polyphonic choral sheet music, and right beside the piano bench a small oak side table displaying Clive's open lined diary filled with crossed-out time-stamped lines ('8:31 AM: Now I am really awake' / '8:35 AM: NOW I am completely awake!') next to a classic porcelain-dial wall clock.

positions.who: Clive Wearing (mannequin in neat British tweed cardigan over collared shirt and tie)
positions.where: seated at the walnut upright piano with expressive, poised hands playing complex choral chords effortlessly from the score — seconds after penning and crossing out a timestamp in his open diary

positions.who: Barbara Wilson & Deborah Wearing (mannequins in 1995 cardigan and blazer)
positions.where: standing warmly beside the piano watching seamless musical mastery outlive a 7-second episodic window

props.name: lined time-stamped diary ('8:31 AM ~~awake~~ -> 8:35 AM NOW truly awake!') & fountain pen
props.period_detail: makes the 7-to-30-second episodic reset heartbreakingly concrete on the page

props.name: walnut upright piano & polyphonic Renaissance choral score
props.physical_behavior: dramatic side-by-side dissociation on one screen

actions.verb_sequence: glances puzzled at his own crossed-out 8:31 AM diary line and writes '8:35 AM: NOW completely awake!' -> turns toward the open choral score on the piano -> hands glide onto the keys playing a rich, flawless Renaissance cadence
sings harmony beside him as Clive conducts her entrance right on the beat

reactions.reaction: radiant, completely whole and authoritative while inside the flow of music
documents 100% preserved procedural artistry alongside 7-second episodic span

scenes.wardrobe: 1995 British knit cardigan, collared shirt and striped tie; smart-casual blazer and warm sweater.
scenes.lighting: Warm, bright tall-window English morning light.
scenes.recognition_hook: Four inches to his left sits a diary where memory resets every twenty seconds — put his hands on piano keys and centuries of music pour out unbroken.

key_visual.description: a sunlit music room where a seated conductor plays choral sheet music on a walnut upright piano right beside a side table holding an open diary of crossed-out timestamps

scenes.title: The Thirty-Second Hallway Reunion: Unbroken Love

layout.description: Bright doorway opening into Clive's sitting room.

positions.where: stepping back into the room holding two cups of tea just 30 seconds after stepping out
rising immediately with outstretched arms and overwhelming joy as if welcoming her home after decades away

props.name: tea tray & open doorway
props.physical_behavior: proves limbic attachment needs zero episodic timestamps

actions.verb_sequence: steps back across threshold -> Clive beams and embraces her immediately

scenes.recognition_hook: Step outside for thirty seconds and he forgets you visited — step back through the door and his heart recognizes you in a tenth of a second.

scenes.title: 2008 20-Year Follow-Up: Feet Know the Kitchen When Words Say 'Zero'

layout.description: Bright tidy flat hallway leading to a small kitchenette with a kettle.

positions.where: walking unhesitatingly down the corridor straight to the kettle to make coffee while verbally insisting he has never seen this building before

props.name: electric kettle & coffee mug
props.period_detail: 20 years of repetition stamped implicit navigation into intact basal ganglia

actions.verb_sequence: walks straight to the right cupboard and fills the kettle without searching

reactions.reaction: notes calm, peaceful implicit adaptation over two decades

scenes.recognition_hook: Ask him verbally where the kitchen is and he has zero idea — ask if he'd like coffee and his feet walk straight to the kettle.

scenes.title: Connecting Through Music & Warmth in Everyday Memory Care
scenes.era: Modern family living room / memory-care music circle

layout.description: Sunlit living room where an adult daughter plays a familiar melody with her older father instead of quizzing dates.

positions.where: singing and tapping rhythm happily together at a keyboard

props.name: songbook of beloved melodies
props.period_detail: activates spared musical and emotional circuits in dementia care
props.physical_behavior: compassionate takeaway from Clive & Deborah Wearing

actions.verb_sequence: closes the calendar quiz and plays the opening chord -> Father joins in smiling on beat one

reactions.reaction: shared joy in the present moment

scenes.recognition_hook: Stop quizzing broken calendars — music and emotional warmth stay open long after dates fade.
